subject: Clarifying proration & buffer behavior for short/ephemeral sessions
messages:

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Question on billing for lots of short calls / proration examples

Hi Mina,

Quick one from our procurement team as we prep the scoping docs: Acme's in-store personalization prototype will make many very short requests — e.g., 30–120 token prompts that run for <1s each, often triggered per customer interaction. We want to align on how Redwood bills these ephemeral calls so we can model cost accurately.

Specifically can you confirm: 
- Do you bill each request separately or do you aggregate small requests within a time window before rounding?
- If you round up, what is the billing quantum? Any minimum per-request charge?
- Is there a buffer/housekeeping token overhead (e.g., for KV cache, prefixing) that we should include in our estimates?

I've attached our procurement questionnaire and a tiny example usage trace. Examples in spreadsheet would be super helpful — even a few sample calculations (25 token prompt, 80 token prompt, repeated 3x/second) so we can show finance.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Liu
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Retail

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Question on billing for lots of short calls / proration examples

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear examples and the attachment. Short answer: we charge per-request token usage, but there are a couple of layers that affect the effective billed tokens for very short, high-frequency calls. I'll outline the pattern and attach a small spreadsheet with worked examples.

High-level summary:
- Accounting unit: tokens are counted per request (prompt + completion). At metering time we apply an aggregation step (see below) and then round to the billing quantum.
- Aggregation window: by default we aggregate token counts for requests coming from the same session/client key over a 60-second window for the purpose of applying the minimum/quantum rounding. This prevents many tiny requests from paying large rounding penalties.
- Billing quantum: we round the aggregated token total up to the nearest 8-token quantum for hosted customers. This is a platform default and configurable on enterprise contracts.
- Buffer overhead: typical protocol/prefix and KV housekeeping adds ~6–12 tokens per request depending on model and instruction formatting. For very short prompts that matters — our attached examples include a conservative +10 token buffer.

I'll let Karthik add the low-level examples and Vanessa/Ben chime in on commercial options (pilot pricing / temporary overrides). Attached: pricing_model_v3.xlsx with three scenarios.

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: pricing_model_v3.xlsx (XLSX spreadsheet)

Subject: Re: Question on billing for lots of short calls / proration examples

Thanks — quick technical addendum with explicit math. I'll keep examples small so finance can paste them into the model. We assume the default +10 token buffer Mina noted and the 60s aggregation window and 8-token quantum.

Scenario A — single tiny prompt (one request):
- Prompt tokens: 25
- Buffer: +10
- Request total: 35 tokens
- Aggregation: single request within window => 35 tokens aggregated
- After rounding to 8-token quantum => round up to 40 billed tokens
- Billing: 40 tokens * price_per_token

Scenario B — repeated short calls (3 calls in 60s):
- Calls: three requests of 25 tokens prompt each
- Raw tokens: 25*3 = 75
- Buffer: +10 per request => +30 => aggregated raw = 105 tokens
- Aggregation: within 60s window we sum => 105 tokens
- Rounding (8-token quantum) => round up to 112 billed tokens

Scenario C — mixed lengths, high frequency (25t, 120t, 25t repeated):
- Raw prompt tokens: 25 + 120 + 25 = 170
- Buffers: +10 per request => +30 => total 200 tokens
- Rounding => round up to 200 (already multiple of 8) => billed 200 tokens

Notes:
- If you disable the aggregation window (enterprise option) we bill each request individually — that can increase effective rounding loss for many tiny requests.
- For Redwood Dedicated/Private customers we can set quantum to smaller values (e.g., 4 tokens) in the contract if needed.

Hope this helps — happy to add a fourth row comparing "no aggregation" vs our default.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Applied Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sara — quick commercial note. For pilots we often offer a temporary aggregation override and a 20% pilot discount on token unit price for the first 90 days to reduce cost risk while you validate the in-store experience. Two options we can propose to Acme: 

Option 1 — Pilot-friendly: keep default aggregation & quantum but give 20% unit price discount for 90 days.
Option 2 — Low-rounding Pilot: enable 4-token quantum + aggregation override for 90 days and give 10% discount on unit price.

If either looks acceptable I can add pricing lines to the quote. We can also show a modeled monthly cost using Karthik's scenarios so your finance team can pick.

—Ben

Sara — attaching a CSV with the requested monthly rollups (50k/day Scenario B) and a one-page summary that shows the three commercial options side-by-side. Quick answers inline: the default 60-second aggregation is applied per client_key. For your per-device client keys that means aggregation will operate independently per device (good for edge cases where devices are rate-limited).

Summary of the 50k/day Scenario B (30d) using our example numbers and a placeholder unit price of $0.000015 per token (we used this for modeling only):
- Default behavior (60s aggregation, 8-token quantum): billed tokens/day ≈ 112 * 50,000 = 5,600,000 tokens/day => monthly ≈ 168,000,000 tokens => estimated $2,520/month before discounts.
- Pilot-friendly (20% off unit price): estimated $2,016/month.
- Low-rounding pilot (4-token quantum + 10% off): billed tokens/day ≈ 100 * 50,000 => monthly ≈ 150,000,000 tokens => estimated $2,025/month.

I've uploaded the calculation CSV and an editable pricing sheet to HubSpot and added the DocuSign PO link if you want to move forward quickly: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/contact/8899 (calc + sheet) and https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcdef-123456
